claims.short_claim: Bounded physical quantum query advantage for compiler-synthesized search problems.
allowed_wording: Q-Psi demonstrated compiler-enabled physical quantum query advantage on structured search problems on IBM Heron hardware under a black-box verifier model.
Quantum query reduction factors of 2.43x (N=4), 1.73x (N=8), and 1.19x (N=16) observed on physical quantum hardware (ibm_marrakesh).
prohibited_wording: General quantum speedup for arbitrary software repair.
End-to-end wall-clock compiler runtime advantage.
General quantum advantage.
claims.qualification: Valid only under the query complexity metric on tested structured oracle families; does not establish wall-clock speedup or general quantum advantage.

claims.short_claim: Bounded physical quantum query complexity advantage on Dynamic Bernstein-Vazirani scaling series.
allowed_wording: Demonstrated statistically significant physical quantum query scaling advantage on Dynamic Bernstein-Vazirani problem across N=4..16 qubits on IBM Marrakesh.
Quantum query scaling slope (0.153) is statistically superior to classical exhaustive bound (0.696, t = -30.65, p < 1e-6).
prohibited_wording: General quantum supremacy.
General quantum advantage for arbitrary computational problems.
claims.qualification: Restricted to the tested oracle complexity model on synthetic scaling series.

claims.short_claim: Mid-circuit measurement and reset reduces physical qubit footprint by median 78.1% with non-inferior observable quality.
allowed_wording: Dynamic mid-circuit qubit reuse compiler passes reduce active physical register width by up to 87.5% (median 78.1%) on streaming and bounded-treewidth circuits without observable degradation (6/6 non-inferior cases).
Evaluated 16 logical-qubit workloads on 2 to 3 physical slots on IBM Marrakesh.
prohibited_wording: 16-qubit quantum computation generally requires only 2 qubits for all algorithms.
Universal width reduction for arbitrary quantum circuits.
claims.qualification: Applicable strictly to circuits with sequential liveness graphs and streaming communication topologies; arbitrary non-local entanglement requires full register width.

claims.short_claim: Physical-QPU-assisted code data generation pipeline feasibility demonstrated with 127.58 quantum seconds on Heron r2.
allowed_wording: Physical QPU sampling on IBM Marrakesh (127.58s runtime, 332,768 shots across 4 jobs) causally selected candidate mutation states, yielding 93 verified positive code repair records (1.59 MB) passing rigorous classical unit and integration verifiers.
Demonstrates mechanical end-to-end pipeline feasibility for quantum-assisted synthetic data generation.
prohibited_wording: Quantum-trained LLMs achieve superior coding performance.
Proven language model improvement from quantum synthetic data.
Quantum data foundry generates 1000s of verified records per second without qualification.
claims.qualification: Feasibility demonstration only. The current throughput bottleneck is classical verification (158 candidates evaluated of 65k QPU states). Downstream LLM fine-tuning and model improvement were NOT tested.

claims.short_claim: Independent cross-compiler benchmark on MQT suite shows mixed competitiveness against Qiskit O3 and TKET.
allowed_wording: On standard MQT benchmarks on IBM Marrakesh, Q-Psi achieves 18/18 valid compilations, ties or competes with Qiskit/TKET across most workloads, exhibits a large advantage over TKET on vqe_su2_n8, but remains physically disfavored vs Qiskit on qft_n6.
Commercial benchmark classification: MIXED_COMPETITIVENESS.
prohibited_wording: Q-Psi universally outperforms Qiskit or TKET.
General compiler superiority across all quantum algorithms.
claims.qualification: Aggregate physical advantage over TKET (+0.0398 delta) is driven by TKET's mapping failure on vqe_su2_n8 (+0.2696); omitting vqe_su2_n8 results in -0.0062 delta. Q-Psi is physically disfavored vs Qiskit (-0.0067 delta).

claims.short_claim: Dynamic ancilla routing improves gate depth but shows no physical fidelity crossover over unitary SWAP chains on Heron r2.
allowed_wording: Dynamic routing structurally compresses 2Q depth from 73 to 2 on long distances (13 hops), but hardware reset and measurement noise prevent a physical Bell fidelity crossover on IBM Marrakesh, confirming pre-QPU compiler predictions.
prohibited_wording: Dynamic routing always outperforms unitary routing on current hardware.
Quantum routing advantage.
claims.qualification: Unitary routing physically wins on short and medium distances; long distance (13 hops) is statistically inconclusive (-0.0314 delta).

claims.short_claim: Hardware-fit compiler optimization achieves exact classical parity for small instances (N<=10) on Heron r2.
allowed_wording: QAOA-based compiler optimization on IBM Marrakesh achieves 4/4 exact optimum hits on small compiler graphs (N<=10), matching classical branch-and-bound, but degrades on N=18..25 due to hardware noise.
prohibited_wording: Quantum compiler optimization outpaces classical solvers.
Quantum advantage for compiler optimization.
claims.qualification: Small graph parity only; large graphs degrade under unmitigated NISQ error.

claims.short_claim: Historical Data Foundry V1 proof-of-concept baseline.
allowed_wording: Initial feasibility demonstration of physical QPU selector on M=1024 space yielding 14 verified unique code repair records.
prohibited_wording: Headline data generation result.
claims.qualification: Proof-of-concept run; superseded by V2 120-Qsec campaign.

claims.short_claim: Q-Psi calibration-aware layout does not outperform strong Qiskit O3 best-of-8 seed baseline on Heron r2.
allowed_wording: Against a strong baseline of Qiskit O3 best-of-8 seeds, Q-Psi calibration-aware layout achieves 1 win, 2 losses, 3 inconclusive (mean delta -0.0106), demonstrating that Qiskit multi-seed search remains superior or competitive on Heron r2.
prohibited_wording: Q-Psi calibration layout outperforms Qiskit layout on IBM Heron.
Compiler layout advantage over Qiskit.
claims.qualification: Negative comparator study preserved for scientific integrity; demonstrates rigorous external baseline comparison.

claims.short_claim: Fractional pulse gate lowering reduces pulse duration structurally but yields mixed physical fidelity improvements.
allowed_wording: Fractional gate lowering yields structural gate duration reductions and 2/6 physical wins (N4_B, N8_B), with 4/6 cases inconclusive on IBM Marrakesh, supporting mixed physical signal.
prohibited_wording: Universal fidelity improvement from fractional pulse lowering.
Pulse-level quantum advantage.
claims.qualification: Only 2/6 cases were conclusive; physical advantage is workload-dependent.

claims.short_claim: Selective Pauli twirling reduces randomized compilation overhead by median 58.9% with mixed fidelity retention.
allowed_wording: Risk-mass layer selection selects only 41.1% of CZ layers for twirling on IBM Directed Execution beta mode; yields 1/4 win vs unmitigated RAW baseline and statistically inconclusive comparison vs full twirling.
prohibited_wording: Selective twirling proven superior to full randomized compiling.
Directed execution advantage.
claims.qualification: Selective vs full non-inferiority was not statistically established across 4 cases; retains mixed signal.

claims.short_claim: Restricted Simon physical study achieves polynomial query reduction on recovered instances but inconclusive asymptotic advantage.
allowed_wording: Physical execution on IBM Marrakesh recovered secrets on 6/12 instances (N=8..28) with polynomial query count reduction relative to classical bound, but noise-induced degradation on larger N prevents establishing asymptotic quantum speedup.
prohibited_wording: Demonstrated asymptotic quantum speedup for Simon's algorithm.
Unconditional physical quantum advantage.
claims.qualification: Inconclusive due to 6/12 recovery failures at higher N under hardware noise.

claims.short_claim: Early exploratory benchmark on static BV and mantra state encoding.
allowed_wording: Exploratory hardware calibration run on static BV and mantra state encoding on IBM Marrakesh.
prohibited_wording: Algorithmic quantum advantage on static BV.

claims.short_claim: Multi-backend retargeting across 3 IBM Heron r2 backends with 5/6 top-tier selection accuracy.
allowed_wording: Across six canonical workloads and three IBM Heron r2 backends, Q-Psi successfully retargeted all 18 workload-backend combinations.
Its frozen pre-QPU selection heuristic selected a backend in the physically best statistical tier for 5/6 workloads.
prohibited_wording: Multi-provider portability.
Cross-vendor compiler independence.
General backend-selection superiority.
Universal compiler advantage.
General quantum advantage.
Best backend selected on 5/6 workloads.
claims.qualification: Tested on three IBM Heron r2 backends from one provider and one processor family. This does not establish multi-provider portability, universal backend-selection superiority, general compiler advantage, or general quantum advantage.
claims.qpu: ibm_fez, ibm_kingston, ibm_marrakesh (IBM Heron r2, 156 programmable qubits)

claims.short_claim: General quantum advantage for arbitrary classical software or compilation tasks.
allowed_wording: General quantum advantage is NOT established by Q-Psi research.
prohibited_wording: Q-Psi has achieved general quantum advantage.
Quantum computers outperform classical computers on general software tasks.
claims.qualification: Explicitly rejected across the entire research program.

claims.short_claim: General compiler runtime or optimization superiority over industrial compiler frameworks.
allowed_wording: General compiler superiority over industrial toolchains (Qiskit, TKET) is NOT established.
prohibited_wording: Q-Psi is universally superior to Qiskit and TKET.
claims.qualification: Explicitly disclaimed; results show specialized advantages and strong baseline parity.
